post.description:
Idempotent: triggers `Orchestrator::cancel_turn` if the run belongs to this
conversation and a matching token is registered, otherwise no-op. The cancel
also covers a turn no worker has claimed yet: its stream ends at once with
`agent_error {"reason":"cancelled","user_message_persisted":false}`. Always returns 200 with the current turn
status — the cancellation propagates asynchronously through the worker's
`tokio::select!`, the SSE stream's terminal `agent_error` event, and the
`event_store`. Clients should poll `GET .../status` (or wait for the
stream's `agent_error`) to observe the transition.

post.description:
The turn's owner answers a pending interaction. The answer is validated by
the interaction kind's handler. Answering is a compare-and-set on `pending`:
repeating the same answer returns `200` with the stored resolution, a
different answer after resolution returns `409`, and an expired or
cancelled interaction (or one whose turn process stopped waiting) returns
`410`.

get.description:
Replays stored events from `?since` (default 0), then tails live events
if the run is still active. Closes when the run finishes, not at the
`done` or `agent_error` frame: events such as `suggestions` follow `done`.
A client that disconnects stops the tail at once.

Returns `404` if no events exist for `run_id` and the run is not active
(never started, unknown, or pruned after the TTL elapsed).

After `done` the stream may carry one `suggestions` frame
(`SseSuggestionsEvent`) with follow-up prompts for the finished turn; it
then closes when the run finishes.

same permissions as `PUT`. Removing a row that does not exist succeeds.

no `allow` rows left it is offered to every space again, except those that
opted out.

post.description:
Uses the credential the caller's turns would use: the shared one, or their
own for a per-user integration. A personal integration can be tested only
by its owner. A failed connection is still a `200` with `ok: false` and the
error, and marks the integration `unreachable` until a connection works.
The error names a kind (`HTTP <status>`, `timeout`, `connection failed`,
`protocol error`), never the raw transport error. An integration can be
tested once every few seconds per caller (`429` with `Retry-After`).
